summary.tpReason: MailGuard corroborates the quarantined message as Phish (92 confidence), with SPF/DKIM/DMARC failures and a macro-enabled .docm. The same infrastructure, 198.51.100.42 and malicious-infra.xyz, sent an allowed phish to mirage@pkwork.onmicrosoft.com four minutes earlier; that account was then used from the same IP across Okta, AWS, and GCP.
summary.fpReason: There is no benign explanation for the linked sequence of foreign sign-in, MFA manipulation, persistent-account creation, cloud resource changes, sensitive-object reads, and logging evasion. The admin recipient's message was contained, but it is part of a confirmed malicious campaign.
summary.whatHappened: At 2026-08-19 06:54:26Z, MailGuard quarantined a phishing email from noreply@malicious-infra.xyz (198.51.100.42) to admin@pkwork.onmicrosoft.com, subject “RE: Meeting Notes — Please Review Attachment,” with meeting-notes.docm. The same IP/domain sent an allowed Phish to mirage@pkwork.onmicrosoft.com at 06:50:37Z with report.exe and a payload URL. At 07:36Z, mirage signed into Okta from 198.51.100.42 (RU), elevated privileges, created an API token, and altered MFA. AWS and GCP were then accessed as mirage: persistence accounts were created, GPU instances launched, cloud data objects read, and logging disabled/deleted.
keyEvidence: MailGuard record at 06:54:26Z confirms the admin message was inbound Phish, Quarantine, 92 confidence, sandbox-scanned, carrying meeting-notes.docm; SPF, DKIM, and DMARC all failed.
At 06:50:37Z, 198.51.100.42 / malicious-infra.xyz delivered an Allowed Phish to mirage@pkwork.onmicrosoft.com with report.exe and https://update-service-cdn.xyz/payload.

Okta logs show successful mirage@pkwork.onmicrosoft.com login from 198.51.100.42 (RU) at 07:36Z, followed by super-admin grant, API-token creation, MFA resets/deactivation, and attacker TOTP enrollment.

AWS CloudTrail records non-MFA mirage access from 198.51.100.42 creating backdoor-svc/access keys/login profile, granting AdministratorAccess, opening 0.0.0.0/0 ingress, launching five p3.16xlarge instances, reading S3 finance/HR/API-key objects, and deleting CloudTrail.

GCP audit logs show mirage from 198.51.100.42 created and granted Owner to backdoor-svc-gcp, opened all ingress, created GPU crypto-miner instances, read financial/PII/API-key objects, and disabled/deleted logging sinks.
researchDone: Queried MailGuard365_Threats_CL and SEG_MailGuard_CL for the message ID, sender, sender IP, attachment hash, sender-domain campaign scope, and both recipients; only MailGuard contained the relevant campaign records.

Queried Azure AD sign-ins for admin and mirage in the 48-hour window; no records were returned. Queried Office activity for both users; no OfficeActivity events were returned. The inbox-rule table could not be time-filtered because its exposed schema lacks TimeGenerated.

Queried SecurityAlert for linked accounts/IOCs and identified corroborating Okta, AWS, and GCP detections; then validated them against the underlying OktaV2_CL, AWSCloudTrail, and GCPAuditLogs events.

Queried CrowdStrike detections and Windows SecurityEvent for mirage, the payload URL, IP, and file hash; no matching endpoint telemetry was returned. AzureActivity_CL also returned no matching Azure actions.
Public web searches for malicious-infra.xyz returned no results; the supplied docm SHA-256 appears to be a placeholder/example value and was not relied upon.
